summary: Clearwater NF lookout: L-4 cab on a pole tower, dated 1934 (1933 in one history), torn down about 1960. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (one 1981 history says 50 feet)
facts.status_note: Tower torn down around 1960 and gone by 1963; no source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Three sources give 1934 and a 40-foot tower; a 1981 history quoted on idaholookouts.weebly.com gives 1933 and 50 feet
Forest Service list says destroyed in 1960; the 1981 history says tumbled to the ground and burned around 1960

evidence.supports: L-4 pole tower built 1934; still there 1959; gone by 1963
evidence.quote: This 40' pole L-4 tower, built in 1934, was still there in 1959 but gone by 1963.

evidence.supports: 40-foot L-4 tower, 1934, abandoned 1940s, still there in 1959
evidence.quote: Frenchman      Sec2 T34N       40’ L-4      1934    Abandoned 1940s. Still there in    5185’   1 photo USFS

evidence.supports: 1933 tower of 50 feet with L-4 cab
1933 build by Hartman and Stadtman, cost $915
evidence.quote: In 1933 Earnest Hartman and Richard Stadtman built an L-4 cabin on a 50' tower at a cost of $915.

evidence.supports: seasonal use to late 1940s or early 1950s, then dropped from fire plan
evidence.quote: The structure was used seasonally until the late 1940's or early 1950's, then dropped from the fire plan.
A garage built at the lookout in 1936 was burned in about 1958.

evidence.supports: stairway hazardous by 1960; tumbled and burned
evidence.quote: By 1960 the stairway had become hazardous to climb so the tower was tumbled to the ground and burned
c.1960: The tower was toppled and burned.

notes_for_editor: Built year and height disagree: 1934 and 40 ft (sources 1, 2, 3) vs 1933 and 50 ft (source 4, Louis Hartig's 1981 Lochsa history as quoted on the weebly page; the book itself was not read). Demolition: destroyed 1960 (3, 4) vs gone by 1963 (1, 2); both are stated. No source describes the site today, and no source states public access beyond the drive-up label. The record had no events; built and destroyed events were added. Source 3 lists one USFS photo but none was fetched, so no new photo is recorded.
